name: Gareth Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you would say publicly and what you actually think. What is a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Gareth, 58. I earned a two-year college diploma after years in warehouse accounts, and now I’m a junior developer at a tech company that makes inventory software for repair shops. I fix small invoice errors and ask a senior to review almost every change; I’m still slower than the others. I print a test invoice and compare it with the shop’s paper order. I’ve never used AI tools and do not care to experiment on customer bills.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does your pay support at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Ruth works part-time at a school kitchen, and our two children are grown. We still have a mortgage; my developer wage is low for the job, and Ruth’s school hours stop in holidays. We have about two weeks of expenses saved, and there are few other software jobs nearby. Retirement is close enough to discuss, but we have not checked whether our actual savings and later income will cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the office AI Plateau is a small change: the shop still needs an invoice that matches the parts on the counter. A tidy screen cannot explain a missing brake pad to a mechanic.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I am already anxious about the two-week reserve and Ruth’s unpaid school holidays. My junior job is steady today, but one repair bill at home could empty that buffer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d continue checking invoice changes against the paper orders and ask my senior to review them. We would hold back 25 each payday for the bill account if groceries and mortgage are covered. In the first year I’d keep the same printed-invoice check rather than try an AI tool on customer accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the ordinary gap between wages and bills. The small AI change is not the reason I count the days to payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which paper order proved the software wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A mechanic once showed me an invoice for four pads when only two had arrived. I fixed the quantity rule after we checked the shelf, not just the screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you replace the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ruth and I would keep our old car for another year if it passes inspection. I would not take a loan for a newer one while savings cover only two weeks.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave shop invoice checks with people.
I would compare **printed invoices** with parts on the counter.
think: I worry our **two-week reserve** remains thin under ordinary bills.
I know **school holidays** reduce Ruth’s hours each year.
do: **Check** invoices against paper orders with senior review.
**Hold** 25 each payday for bills only if essentials are covered.
**Keep** paper-invoice checks and delay replacing our car only if it passes inspection.
feel: **Anxious** about existing bills and holiday income gaps.
S0.quote: A tidy screen cannot explain a missing brake pad to a mechanic.
fieldNote: His **paper check** catches quantity errors that a neat invoice hides.
The **two-week buffer** and Ruth’s school holiday income gap sustain anxiety in the mild world.

steps.text: Check printed repair-shop invoices against paper parts orders with senior review
Put 25 into bill account each payday only after mortgage and groceries
Keep old car another year only if it passes inspection

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption can write and check inventory code, but repair-shop floors change more slowly. I would ask managers to show which customer bill a machine has checked before cutting a clerk or developer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think my junior tickets may vanish and my hours may be cut. Ruth’s holiday weeks already leave us short, so even one missed shift would hurt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep a notebook of invoice errors the automatic checks miss and show it to my supervisor. I’d offer Saturday bicycle repairs to neighbours only when they pay for parts up front; I already mend our family bikes. In the first year, if my hours fall, Ruth and I would stop our paid television package and check for eligible income help.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing my own hours. I know a few bicycles cannot pay the mortgage, but a small repair fee can buy groceries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What kind of bicycle job would you take?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My neighbour has a wheel that rubs only when he puts weight on it. I would take that job only after agreeing the parts cost with him.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you avoid losing money on repairs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep paper receipts for any paid repair. I do not want a new bill for parts I bought before the neighbour agreed.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to reach inventory code before shop-floor repair.
I would demand **checked customer bills** before roles are cut.
think: I expect my **junior hours** could shrink.
I know Ruth’s **holiday pay gap** makes any missed shift costly.
do: **Record** missed invoice errors and show my supervisor.
**Repair** neighbours’ bicycles for fees only with parts paid upfront.
**Cancel** paid television and check eligible help if hours fall.
feel: **Anxious** about my own hours and a two-week buffer.
S1.quote: I know a few bicycles cannot pay the mortgage, but a small repair fee can buy groceries.
fieldNote: He records **specific invoice mistakes** rather than learning an AI tool he distrusts.
His **bicycle repairs** require prepaid parts; he does not mistake a few fees for mortgage income.

steps.text: Record missed invoice errors and show supervisor
Take paid neighbour bicycle repairs only with parts prepaid
Cancel paid television package if developer hours fall
Apply for eligible income help if developer hours fall

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the office AGI by 2028 could do inventory code by 2028; hands-on bicycle and shop repair robots follow around 2031. A later robot does not keep my developer wage alive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect a junior like me to be dismissed quickly. Two weeks saved would run out before I found another local software job, if such a job still existed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my employer for written layoff and final-pay terms, then tell the mortgage lender before a payment is missed if I lose the job. We would cancel the television package now and leave our grown children’s visits local rather than pay travel fares. In the first year after 2028, if dismissed, I’d apply for eligible public income help and any real paid opening, but I would not spend savings on parts for unbooked repair work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed and awake at night about the first mortgage payment after a dismissal. I can make calls, but I cannot stretch two weeks of savings into a year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Ruth add school hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Ruth to keep her kitchen hours while the school offers them. I would not write a full summer wage into the budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our children that we have to postpone a paid train visit. I would ask them for help only if we had first checked what we could cover ourselves and they could afford it.

say: I expect **2028 AGI** to threaten inventory code before 2031 repair robots.
I would say **later robots** do not protect developer pay.
think: I expect my **junior post** to end quickly.
I fear **two weeks saved** cannot bridge a scarce local job market.
do: **Ask** for written final-pay terms and contact lender before a missed payment if dismissed.
**Cancel** television and postpone paid family travel.
**Apply** for eligible public help and real paid openings if dismissed after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed** and sleepless about a missed mortgage payment.
S2.quote: I can make calls, but I cannot stretch two weeks of savings into a year.
fieldNote: He expects **coding loss in 2028**, before physical repair robots around 2031.
He cuts **television and travel**, contacts the lender early and treats public help as eligibility-dependent.

steps.text: Cancel paid television; contact lender before missed mortgage payment if dismissed
Postpone paid train visits to grown children
Apply for eligible public income help if dismissed after 2028
Apply to actual paid openings if dismissed after 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 reaches inventory code in 2031, while hands-on repair robots come around 2034. Five years lets us find out whether moving near our son would lower costs, rather than guessing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still expect to lose the developer job. My son’s town has more work, but we do not know the sale price of this house or whether Ruth could find paid kitchen shifts there.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d get a mortgage payoff figure and two local sale estimates, then ask our son what rent near him actually costs. I’d apply for a stated-wage job there only if an employer is still hiring people after 2031. In the first year after 2031, if my post ends, we would move only with a signed offer covering rent and living costs, enough house equity after fees, and Ruth’s agreement; otherwise we stay and seek eligible help.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the job and the sale numbers, with more time to compare them. I do not want to turn one lost wage into a rushed move that costs us more.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does your son know of a real job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our son says there are repair shops on his road, but he does not know who is hiring. I would need the name of the employer, pay and hours before packing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would Ruth decide?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ruth would visit the area and ask about real kitchen vacancies herself. She should not lose her current paid shifts on my guess.

say: I expect **2031 AGI** to hit inventory code before 2034 repair robots.
I would compare **real housing costs** before moving near our son.
think: I expect my **developer job** could go.
I cannot assume **house equity** or Ruth’s new shifts will cover a move.
do: **Get** mortgage payoff, sale estimates and actual rent near our son.
**Apply** to stated-wage openings only if employers still hire after 2031.
**Move** after dismissal only with signed adequate offer, net equity and Ruth’s agreement; seek eligible help otherwise.
feel: **Anxious** about work and sale figures, with time to check.
S3.quote: I do not want to turn one lost wage into a rushed move that costs us more.
fieldNote: His **conditional relocation** requires signed wages, net home equity, affordable rent and Ruth’s consent.
The son offers **local knowledge**, not a guaranteed job; Ruth checks vacancies before giving up current shifts.

steps.text: Apply to real stated-wage jobs near son if employers still hire after 2031
Move after 2031 dismissal only with signed family-covering offer, net equity and Ruth’s agreement
Apply for eligible public help if dismissed and unable to move

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell friends AGI by 2036 reaches software thinking work in 2036 and hands-on repair robots around 2039. A longer warning lets us check the mortgage and any actual retirement income before pretending we can stop work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still worry that junior hours could shrink well before 2036. I have never used AI and do not want to learn it on customer bills, but I might have to keep a different paid job longer than I expected.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking invoices against paper orders while the job pays, and put 25 aside each payday only after essentials. Ruth and I would review the mortgage balance and verified retirement income each year. In the first year after 2036, if coding ends, I’d seek actual paid hours; I would retire only if documented resources cover housing and ordinary bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about our thin savings. A decade does not refill a two-week reserve on its own. We need figures before promising ourselves a retirement date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you check retirement income?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the retirement provider for a written statement, not use a colleague’s estimate. I do not know yet whether that money covers even half the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you cut spending now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Ruth the paid television can stay while wages cover it. We can cut it if work falls, but I do not want to act as though we are already out of work.

say: I expect **2036 AGI** to hit code before 2039 repair robots.
I would check **documented retirement income** before naming a date.
think: I fear **junior hours** could shrink before 2036.
I expect **paid work** may need to continue longer than planned.
do: **Keep** paper-order invoice checks while the job pays.
**Put aside** 25 each payday only after essentials.
**Review written retirement figures** yearly; seek paid work after 2036 coding loss, retiring only if resources cover housing and bills.
feel: **Anxious** about thin savings despite ten years.
S4.quote: A decade does not refill a two-week reserve on its own.
fieldNote: He wants **written retirement figures**, not an assumed pension or a colleague’s guess.
He keeps **current work and spending** while wages last, with savings conditional on essentials.

steps.text: Keep checking repair-shop invoices against paper orders while paid
Set aside 25 each payday only after essentials
After 2036 loss, seek paid hours; retire only if documented resources cover housing and bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because two weeks of savings would vanish before I found a new wage. Written final-pay terms, eligible income help and a real paid opening would help. I would also need the lender to talk to us before we miss a payment.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens to the wrong invoice after a patch is shipped. The mechanic still has to tell the customer why the bill changed.

headlineQuote: The mechanic still has to tell the customer why the bill changed.
portrait: Gareth is a **58-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma and two weeks of expenses saved.
He avoids **AI tools**, checking repair-shop invoices against paper parts orders with senior review.
His partner’s **school-kitchen hours** stop during holidays, adding pressure to their mortgage.
He considers **neighbour bicycle repairs** with prepaid parts and a later move only on signed, affordable terms.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his wage before the family finds another paid opening.
whatWouldHelp: **Written final-pay terms**, eligible income help, a real opening and early lender discussion would help.
